profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point in Siena, Italy, tagged telecom=data_center, is named E. D. Accounting Siena. The word "Accounting" in the business name plainly identifies this as an accounting or bookkeeping practice serving local clients, not a data center or IT hosting business. Accounting firms maintain their own office computing and, in many cases, client financial-record servers, but that is a fundamentally different function from a commercial colocation or cloud data center. The telecom=data_center tag on this point is best explained as a mapping error applied to the firm's own small server room or network closet, and this entry records that determination plainly rather than inventing data-center specifications for an accounting office.

reading.body:
E. D. Accounting Siena is an accounting firm, not a data center, and its OpenStreetMap data center tag is a mapping error.

The name itself carries the evidence. A bookkeeping practice serving local clients keeps office computers and possibly a small server room for client records. That is a different function from a commercial colocation or cloud facility, which sells rack space and power to outside tenants. The telecom=data_center tag most plausibly landed on the firm's own network closet.

The entry matters as a calibration point rather than as capacity. Any count of Italian data centers built from OpenStreetMap tags will include points like this one, so raw tag counts overstate the real footprint. The error runs in the direction of inflation, not omission.

The data records no megawatts, no operator, and no website, which is consistent with a facility that does not exist as a commercial site. It does not tell the reader how many similar mislabeled points remain in the same source, and it says nothing about actual data center capacity in or near Siena.
